text:
Maya Singh: Dropping a new idea for the Autoscale row: add a compact "density" toggle that reduces padding and shows an inline "estimate sparkline" next to the SLO slider. Sketch: https://www.figma.com/file/novel/autoscale-density-proposal. Main goals: keep dashboard rows denser, surface tiny p95 trend + cost delta, and keep keyboard/a11y parity. Owen Brooks: Love the density toggle concept. Concern: tiny sparklines might be invisible to low-vision users. We should have a text fallback like `p95 trend: +3%` and `cost: +6%` exposed via aria. Tara Li: Agree on fallback. Also propose a safety-band overlay on the slider that visually marks guardrail-safe range (hashed pattern). Screen readers should get the numeric safe range: `Safe SLO: 200ms to 500ms` via `aria-describedby`. Marco Ruiz: Microcopy suggestion for the burst badge: instead of "Burst" try "Short burst" for compact mode and tooltip: `Short burst: temporarily uses elastic GPUs (up to X mins) — may increase cost` and an inline note when disabled: `Burst not available on pinned pools`. Use lock icon + text. Maya Singh: Implementation detail: density toggle persists per-user. Pressing it shrinks row height and collapses helper copy into hover/focus popovers. Keyboard users must still access the same info. Owen Brooks: For keyboard: tab -> density toggle -> chevron expand -> slider -> info button -> burst toggle. Info button opens a popover with `Est. p95: 320ms · Cost +8%` and a 1-line explanation. Popover must be focus-trapped and closable with Escape. Tara Li: Accessibility: prefer a single `aria-live="polite"` region for updated estimates rather than per-control live regions. Debounce updates to 300ms. When density mode is on, also announce "Density mode on: helper copy hidden, press i for details". Marco Ruiz: Copy tweak for guardrail warning: current "violates guardrail" is blunt. Suggest: `Guardrail warning: this setting may increase P95 above your target (suggested safe: 450ms).` Add CTA `Apply safe value`. Maya Singh: UX question: should estimate sparklines be interactive? I.e., hover a sparkline to pin the estimate panel so it stays open. I think yes for power users, but must be keyboard operable (Enter to pin). Owen Brooks: Pinning is fine. Make sure pinned state has `aria-pressed` and visible outline. Also add a visible indicator when estimates are stale (small clock icon) and text `estimates based on recent traffic` in the popover. Tara Li: For the compact min/max behavior: when space is tight show `1 — 8` with an inline small button `edit` that expands to steppers. The button needs `aria-expanded` and full descriptive label: `Edit autoscale min and max, currently min 1 max 8`. Marco Ruiz: Edge-case: when the user has both pinned pools and a burst-enabled elastic pool in the same config, show an inline cluster indicator: `Pinned: Pool-A · Elastic: Pool-B (Burst on)` so it's clear which pool allows burst. Maya Singh: Visual: safety-band overlay uses a pattern + 2x contrast border so it's visible in all themes. Also keep focus rings >3:1 contrast. For density mode make sure tappable targets remain >=44px. Owen Brooks: QA checklist idea: test with NVDA/VoiceOver, keyboard-only, high-contrast theme, and mobile zoom @200%. Also test rapid slider scrubbing vs debounced live updates. Tara Li: I'll draft the copy for tooltips/popovers and the offscreen strings for ARIA. Example offscreen: `
Autoscale min 1 max 8. Burst: short burst enabled on elastic pool. Safe SLO range 200ms to 500ms.
` Marco Ruiz: I'll update the figma with density on/off artboards, the sparkline states, pinned-cluster label, and the safety band. Tagging @Tara and @Owen for a11y + interaction review. ETA: EOD tomorrow. :rocket:
